arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] URGENT — why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

I'm sorry for the disruption—being signed out unexpectedly is incredibly frustrating, especially under a deadline.

We don't have an announced policy change that would require signing out of one machine when you log in to another. Under normal circumstances, you should be able to stay signed in on multiple devices with the same Google SSO account, as you have been until recently.

This new behavior may indicate a bug or a security flag being triggered. Since your workflow spans multiple platforms (macOS and Linux, local and remote), it's possible a recent update or an edge case is affecting your account's sign-in sessions.

To help us investigate, could you please let us know if you:
1. Recently changed your Google account password or other security settings.
2. Notice this after any app or OS updates on your devices.

In parallel, I'm flagging this with our team for immediate review. If possible, please reply with the version of Cursor you’re running (Help → About) and a timestamp for your last forced sign-out. This will help us pinpoint what’s going on.

You can find general troubleshooting for Google SSO here: https://localhost:5008/kb/sso-google-signin

Thank you for bringing this to our attention—we take Pro customer workflows seriously, and I will make sure you get a real answer as fast as possible.

Best,
Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Support

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] URGENT — why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

I'm sorry for the disruption—being signed out unexpectedly is incredibly frustrating, especially under a deadline.

We don't have a policy or recent change that would cause you to be signed out of one machine when accessing Cursor from another. Normally, you should be able to remain signed in on multiple devices with the same Google SSO account. The behavior you’re describing sounds like it might be a bug or possibly related to a security check triggered by device activity.

To help investigate, please let us know if you:
1. Recently changed your Google (SSO) password or account security settings.
2. Noticed any updates to Cursor, your browser, or OS just before this started.

If you can, please also reply with your current Cursor version (Help → About) and an approximate timestamp of your last forced sign-out. This additional info will help our engineering team diagnose the issue.

You can also find general SSO troubleshooting steps here: https://localhost:5008/kb/sso-google-signin

Thank you for your patience—a member of our support team will update you as soon as we know more. We know your time is valuable and will treat this with urgency.

Best,
Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Support

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4815] Invoice PDF won't download
arguments.body:
Hi Daniel,

Sorry for the trouble downloading your March invoice. This typically happens when a browser extension or privacy setting blocks the download, or if there is a temporary issue on our end.

Here are a few steps you can try:
1. Open Cursor in a private/incognito window and try downloading the invoice again.
2. Disable any browser extensions related to privacy or security, then refresh and try again.
3. Ensure that cookies for billing.cursor.com are allowed in your browser settings.

If these steps don’t resolve the problem, please let us know which device and browser you’re using, and we’ll escalate the issue to our billing team right away.

Thank you for your patience!

Best,
Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Support

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4820] Feature request: keyboard shortcut for inline edit
arguments.body:
Hi Riya,

Thank you for your suggestion! At this time, Cursor does not have a dedicated keyboard shortcut for triggering inline edit directly—you’re correct that the current way requires using Cmd-K (or Ctrl-K on Windows/Linux) and then clicking.

I’ve recorded your feature request for our product team. We’re always looking for ways to streamline keyboard navigation and reduce friction for power users like you. If this feature gets added in a future version, we’ll include it in the release notes and update the support articles to reflect the new shortcut.

Thanks again for taking the time to share feedback!

Best,
Lyra Support Bot
Cursor Support
